one_liner: Rust SIMD blur crate (Gaussian, stack, box, median); exact large-kernel Gaussian about 4x faster than multithreaded OpenCV GaussianBlur.
what_it_does: Pure-Rust library of image blurs and separable convolutions for interleaved 8-bit, 16-bit and f32 (f16 on nightly) images with 1, 3 or 4 channels: exact Gaussian, stack blur, binomial 'fast gaussian' variants, box/tent/gaussian-box, median, bilateral and fast bilateral, plus generic 1D/2D and FFT filters, Sobel, Laplacian, motion and lens kernels. Calls take a borrowed BlurImage source and a BlurImageMut destination, a params struct (GaussianBlurParams from kernel size and/or sigma), a per-axis EdgeMode2D, a ThreadingPolicy and, for integer Gaussians, a ConvolutionMode (Exact or FixedPoint), and return Result<(), BlurError>. An optional `image` feature adds wrappers over image::DynamicImage. It is not a drop-in for cv::GaussianBlur and has no C API: the repo's cbindgen.toml is empty and lib.rs exports only Rust functions.
how_it_is_fast: The Gaussian is a separable two-pass convolution that folds the symmetric kernel (adds mirrored taps before one multiply, halving multiplies) in hand-written intrinsics for AVX2+FMA and SSE4.1 (chosen at runtime with is_x86_feature_detected), NEON with RDM, SVE and AVX-512 (opt-in) and wasm simd128. Exact mode uses f32 weights with FMA accumulation; FixedPoint mode scales weights to Q15 integers with i32 accumulators. The vertical pass computes 2 output rows (x86) or 3 (NEON) per iteration to reuse loaded rows, kernels of 61 taps or fewer use a sliding row buffer instead of a full transient image, and rows are split into static zones across threads from the author's novtb crate. Stack and box blurs are O(1)-per-pixel running sums; median is a Huang-style sliding 256-bin histogram per channel.
when_to_use: Rust pipelines that need a true Gaussian with large kernels (tens to ~150+ taps) on 8-bit RGB, RGBA or grayscale frames in the 10-12 MP range, run multithreaded, without linking OpenCV.
Code that must run the same SIMD-accelerated blur on x86-64 and aarch64 (Apple silicon, ARM servers), including u16 and f32 images or arbitrary separable kernels.

UI, thumbnail or background-blur work where an approximation is acceptable: stack_blur, fast_gaussian_next and box_blur are the crate's fastest paths (author's speed order: box, stack, fast_gaussian_next, fast_gaussian, ..., gaussian, bilateral, median).
Builds that want pure Rust (no C/C++ toolchain); wasm32 with simd128 is partially covered.
when_not_to_use: When output must match OpenCV bit for bit: weights, intermediate rounding and borders differ (libblur benches use Clamp; OpenCV defaults to reflect-101), and the default ConvolutionMode is the approximate FixedPoint.
From C or C++ without writing your own FFI shim and adding a Rust toolchain; no C header or extern "C" API ships.
Median blur as a speed play: the README shows only 3-16% over OpenCV (derived) and no public harness produces those rows; the per-pixel cost grows with radius (sliding histogram, not Perreault O(1)).
Small kernels or small images: the README publishes no numbers below kernel 151 (the gauss harness has 3- and 13-tap cases but no results), and each multithreaded call spawns fresh threads.
Analysis that needs an analytic Gaussian: the approximations are flagged by the author as unsuitable for advanced analysis, and FixedPoint adds a stated 1-3% error.

integration.dependencies: num-traits, rayon, num-complex, novtb (author's scoped thread-pool crate, which uses core_affinity); optional image 0.25 (feature image) and zaft (feature fft)
integration.min_toolchain: Rust 1.89 for 0.24.0 (rust-version in Cargo.toml, edition 2024); nightly for the sve, nightly_f16 and nightly_fcma features (avx512 needs nightly before 1.89). The repo's own rust-toolchain.toml pins an unversioned nightly.
integration.platforms: x86-64 (SSE4.1 and AVX2+FMA selected at runtime; AVX-512 opt-in feature), aarch64 NEON (RDM on by default; SVE on nightly), wasm32 simd128 partial, scalar fallback elsewhere
integration.thread_safety: Functions are stateless and work on caller-provided buffers. ThreadingPolicy chooses Single, Adaptive (width*height/65536 threads capped at available cores), AdaptiveReserve or Fixed. The ThreadingPolicy docs warn that fast bilateral relies on Rayon and can use excessive memory and CPU when it is called from work already scheduled by an outside Rayon pool; issue #67 reported memory not being released when fast_gaussian_next_f32 ran under Rayon with Adaptive/Fixed (closed with linked PR #68).
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — same operation as cv::GaussianBlur (separable Gaussian from kernel size and sigma, sigma default uses OpenCV's 0.3*((k-1)/2-1)+0.8 formula), but a Rust-only API, different border default and rounding, so results are not bit-identical

gotchas: ConvolutionMode::FixedPoint is the default (doc comment: estimated error not less than 1-2%); pass ConvolutionMode::Exact for f32 weights. In both modes the horizontal pass is stored in the image's own type (u8 for 8-bit) before the vertical pass, so 'Exact' means f32 weights and accumulation, not a float intermediate.
Kernel sizes must be odd: GaussianBlurParams::new with an even size returns BlurError::OddKernel, while new_from_kernel rounds to the nearest odd size and derives sigma.

Every parallel stage of every call spawns new scoped OS threads through novtb and pins them to cores round-robin with core_affinity; this adds spawn cost per call and can collide with other pinned workloads or thread pools.

Kernels are rewritten often: 0.23.0 (2026-02-13) skipped rows in the single-plane FixedPoint Gaussian (issue #86, fixed in 0.23.1 by PR #87 'Fix skipped rows'), and earlier f32 Gaussian artifacts were reported in issues #21 and #38. Pin the version and compare output after upgrades.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick libblur over the C++ Gaussian siblings (LibGaussianBlur, archived in 2024; zanazakaryaie/fastGaussianBlur, a tutorial; bfraboni/FastGaussianBlur, an approximation with no OpenCV comparison) when you can take a Rust dependency and want a maintained exact Gaussian plus fast approximations, u16/f32 support and NEON/AVX kernels in one crate. Pick FastBoxBlur or bfraboni's header-only code when you need a C++ source drop and a box or approximate blur is enough.
verified_claims_summary: First-party criterion runs (app/benches/gauss/main.rs) on two unnamed machines labelled NEON and AVX, against OpenCV 4.x through the opencv crate (version, build and thread count unstated), both multithreaded: the Exact Gaussian on a 3000x4000 RGB 8-bit image with kernel 155 and sigma 25.83 (README says 151) took 49.40/43.41 ms against OpenCV's 180.56/182.44 ms (about 3.7x/4.2x, derived from page data), and on a single 3000x4000 plane 17.59/15.51 ms against 74.73/64.20 ms (about 4.2x/4.1x, derived). OpenCV's 8-bit ALGO_HINT_ACCURATE path here is GaussianBlurFixedPoint, which quantizes kernel weights to 8 fractional bits (ufixedpoint16), so it is bit-exact across platforms but not more precise in its weights than libblur's f32 Exact mode. The README's RGBA Gaussian, stack-blur, box and median rows are not backed by matching harness code, and the tables were last edited in May 2025, before the 2026 kernel rewrites.
status_note: Active: v0.24.0 on crates.io 2026-05-09 (about 101k downloads), last commit 2026-05-08, 685 commits and 0 open issues; dual Apache-2.0/BSD-3-Clause, so copyable, but Rust-only with no C API.
